figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Microbe engineering to provide drimane-type building blocks for meroterpenoid synthesis. (A) Drimane skeleton and representative
drimane-type merosesquiterpenoids (DMT) including pyripyropene C, zonarol (1), ent-(+)-chromazonarol (2), mycoleptodiscin A (3), and pelorol
(4). Drimane cores are highlighted in blue. (B) Classical synthetic strategies of DMT that involve side-chain degradation and enantioselective
polycyclization. (C) An overview of the integrated approach combining microbe engineering and chemical synthesis for DMT production.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Optimization of drimenol production through terpene syn-
thases screening and fusion strategies. (A) Comparison of drimenol
yields using three different bacterial drimenol synthases. A one-way
ANOVA for multiple comparisons was used (*p<0.05). (B) Schematic
of enzyme configurations: single enzyme, separate enzyme units, and
fusion proteins with varying linker lengths (n=0–4). Inset shows linker
compositions. (C) Drimenol yield optimization using various enzyme
arrangements and fusion constructs (n=0–4). Yield differences
between groups were analyzed using an unpaired two-tailed t-test
(****p<0.0001). (D) Predicted structural model of the optimized
SsNDH-SsDMS fusion protein. SsNDH (pink) connected to SsDMS
(orange, with β and γ subunits indicated) via a flexible linker (blue).
Error bars in panels A and C correspond to standard deviation of three
independent replicates.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Engineering of PhoN. (A) PhoN homology model with active site pocket. Inset: key residues within 4 Å of DMAP. (B) Alanine scanning
results of selected residues in (A). (C) Electrostatic surface modifications: wild-type vs. charge-altering mutations. (D) Yield effects of charge-
altering mutations. (E) Surface representation of PhoN colored by evolutionary conservation. (F) Sequence logos of PhoN homologs. Boxed
residues indicate mutation targets. (G) Yield comparisons of conservation-guided mutations. Error bars in panels B, D, and G correspond to
standard deviation of three independent replicates. Yield differences between groups were analyzed using an unpaired two-tailed t-test (*p<0.05;
**p<0.01; ***p<0.001; ****p<0.0001).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Structural analysis of PhoNE122R/T157K/R160K and optimization of albicanol production. (A) Combinatorial effects of mutations on drimenol
yield from Strategy 1 and Strategy 2. Yield differences between groups were analyzed using an unpaired two-tailed t-test (**p<0.01;
****p<0.0001). (B) Crystal structure of PhoNE122R/T157K/R160K. (C) Structural comparison of wild-type PhoN (gray) and PhoNE122R/T157K/R160K (blue).
Inset: mutated residues with DMAP. (D) Molecular dynamics simulations of wild-type PhoN and PhoNE122R/T157K/R160K with DMAP, showing RMSD
values. (E) Albicanol fermentation profile showing OD600, glucose consumption, and albicanol yield over time. Inset: albicanol structure. Error bars
in A correspond to standard deviation of three independent replicates.

Figure 5. Divergent synthesis of DMT from albicanol. (A) Nickel-catalyzed reductive coupling of albicanol (6) and aryl halides (8). (B) Chiral pool
synthesis of zonarol (1), ent-(+)-chromazonarol (2), mycoleptodiscin A (3), and pelorol (4).
